covers: encoded set as fraction of natural amino acids
honest non-derivation of the numerical count
data_sources: Bock, Forchhammer, Heider & Baron, Mol. Microbiol. 5:515-520 (1991)
PubChem / Handbook of Biochemistry amino acid surveys (order-of-magnitude count of natural, non-proteinogenic amino acids)

tests.test: V4.1 the genetically encoded set is a small fraction of the chemically known amino acid space
tests.interpretation: Fewer than one in ten of the several hundred amino acids known to occur in nature are genetically encoded. Corollary 'The encoded set is a recurrence statistic' predicts exactly this asymmetry: the overwhelming majority of chemically possible residues either never arose as a favourable local substitution in any self-propagating lineage, or arose in only one such lineage and were never independently rediscovered, so they never crossed the recurrence threshold of Theorem 'Recurrence is required for a shared category' and were never abstracted into a storable symbol.

tests.test: V4.2 the two recoded residues require dedicated, narrow-context machinery absent for the 20 standard residues
tests.interpretation: Selenocysteine and pyrrolysine are, on independently established biochemical grounds, not decoded by the ordinary, universal codon-assignment mechanism available at every position for the 20 standard residues; each requires additional, dedicated cis-acting sequence elements and trans-acting factors, and each is restricted to a narrow subset of proteins and organisms. This is the real biochemical fingerprint the manuscript's account predicts for a residue that sits past the recurrence threshold of Theorem 'Recurrence is required for a shared category': it can still be genetically specified, but only by machinery dedicated to that one narrow case, rather than by the uniform mechanism that suffices once a residue has achieved the ordinary, cross-lineage recurrence the 20 standard residues achieved.

tests.test: V4.3 the numerical value 22 is reported honestly as a recurrence statistic, not a derived first-principles count
tests.interpretation: The manuscript's Corollary 'The encoded set is a recurrence statistic' explicitly does not compute 22 from the combinatorics of a specific inventory of prebiotic chemical pathways, and Section 'Scope and Open Questions' identifies this computation as outstanding work. This entry records the observed value for completeness and excludes it from the pass/fail tally, since a test that could not have failed is not informative and reporting it as a pass would overstate what has been established.
